transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with these episodes where I eat a massive amount of food in a really short period of time. It feels completely out of my control, and I feel like I just can't stop once I start. I really need help figuring out how to manage this.
After these episodes of overeating, do you engage in any behaviors to try and prevent weight gain, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or excessive exercising?

It's really hard to admit, but yes, I do. Out of sheer panic after eating, I force myself to throw up, fast for days, and force myself to exercise way past my physical limits. Sometimes I even resort to taking laxatives because I'm so desperate to get rid of the food.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Binge-Eating Disorder, Bulimia Nervosa]. The patient confirmed engaging in compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, fasting, excessive exercise, and laxative use) following episodes of overeating. These compensatory behaviors distinguish Bulimia Nervosa from Binge-Eating Disorder, leading to the removal of the latter.
